metadata.title: Broadcom slips on Q4 guide miss, but sees revenue doubling in 2027 and 2028

content.text:
Investing.com -- Broadcom shares slipped nearly 2% in premarket trading Thursday, paring losses after CEO Hock Tan shared predictions of revenue doubling in both 2027 and 2028 during the company's earnings call.
The news helped steady the stock after Broadcom forecasted fourth-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates, raising concerns that intensifying competition in custom artificial intelligence processors could limit growth.
Those growth fears were assuaged when Tan projected the chipmaker's revenue would rise to $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and further double to $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $34.8 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $35.05 billion. Broadcom also forecast fourth-quarter AI chip sales of $21.7 billion, slightly above analysts' estimate of $21.33 billion, highlighting continued strength in its AI business.
"NVDA guided out year revenue for the first time and AVGO chose to take it a step further with a first look at FY28," Barclays analysts led by Tom O'Malley commented. "First and foremost, this should expel concerns of any near-term peak, but it brings into question the "you need to raise it every call" concern. The company explicitly said this would not be updated on a quarterly basis."
Broadcom's custom-chip business faces growing competition as major technology companies seek alternatives to Nvidia's dominant AI processors. Marvell, for example, struck a custom-chip agreement with Google last month that could generate up to $120 billion in revenue through fiscal 2033, while potentially making Google one of Marvell's largest investors through a stake of as much as $12.2 billion.
Broadcom has also been working to expand its manufacturing capacity and reduce dependence on individual suppliers as AI demand strains the semiconductor supply chain. In July, the company signed a multi-year memorandum of understanding with Samsung Electronics as part of those efforts.
For the third quarter, AI chip sales more than tripled to $16.7 billion, helping lift total revenue to $29.59 billion. Adjusted earnings were $3.32 per share, compared with analysts' estimate of $3.21 per share. Revenue also exceeded the $29.25 billion consensus estimate.
The results underscore the strength of Broadcom's AI franchise, but the weaker-than-expected revenue outlook suggests investors are increasingly focused on whether the company can sustain rapid growth as hyperscalers diversify their custom-chip suppliers.
The stock has gained about 6% so far this year, trailing both major semiconductor peers and the broader chip index.
Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.
